text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate lines, and give variables clearer names. This makes the code simpler for other programmers to work with. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up over time when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. By regularly improving code structure, teams can add new features more easily and avoid future problems. Remember, the behavior of the program should stay exactly the same after refactoring.
